topic: Use your card in another state
guidance: If you already have an eligible NFSA card, look for an ePoS-enabled Fair Price Shop in the state where you now live. ONORC lets eligible cardholders use their existing card across states.
relationship: One Nation One Ration Card uses Existing NFSA Card.

guidance: For portability, use your existing eligible AAY or PHH card. The central FAQ says moving to another state does not require surrendering it or getting a new card just for portability.
relationship: Existing NFSA Card supports Portability Claim.

topic: The physical card is back home
guidance: The central FAQ describes using a card copy or quoting the ration card number at an ePoS-enabled shop for portability. The shop still follows the applicable authentication process.
relationship: Card Number supports Portability Claim.

guidance: Ask whether the destination shop supports ONORC transactions on its ePoS device. For portability, the dealer retrieves the entitlement tied to your home-state card.
relationship: Portability Claim requires ePoS-enabled Fair Price Shop.

guidance: The ONORC FAQ describes collecting all or part of the eligible grain entitlement. Check the remaining balance before making another trip to a shop.
relationship: Portability Claim uses Monthly Entitlement.

guidance: Ask the dealer what failed on the device. Check the official state food department or PDS helpline for the procedure applicable to your case. The central FAQ describes biometric authentication for portability.
relationship: ePoS-enabled Fair Price Shop uses Biometric Authentication.

guidance: Ask for the reason, note the shop and date, and open your state or UT’s official complaint portal. The TPDS amendment addresses refusal of ONORC distribution to eligible migrant beneficiaries.
relationship: Ration Refusal supports Complaint Preparation.

guidance: Open the NFSA complaint directory, choose your state or UT and follow its official grievance procedure. Keep any reference number the official portal gives you.
relationship: NFSA Complaint Directory routes to State Grievance Portal.

guidance: The Government of India lists 1967 or a state-specific 1800-series number for PDS complaints. Use the official state directory if the short number does not connect.
relationship: PDS Helpline supports Complaint Preparation.

guidance: The NFSA framework identifies District Grievance Redressal Officers and State Food Commissions. Use your state’s official grievance route to confirm where your case should go.
relationship: District Grievance Officer supports Grievance Review.

topic: Apply for a new ration card
guidance: Use the NFSA application directory and choose your state or UT. The state or UT sets the application procedure and decides who is eligible.
relationship: NFSA Application Directory routes to State Food Portal.

guidance: Start with your state’s Food and Civil Supplies department to check its eligibility rules. The national NFSA portal directs people to state or UT authorities for identification and issuance.
relationship: State Food Portal supports Eligibility Check.

guidance: Open your state’s application page and check its current list of documents before travelling or applying. The national portal routes new applications to the relevant state or UT authority.
relationship: State Food Portal supports Application Checklist.

topic: Check a card record or status
guidance: Choose your state in the NFSA ration card directory to find the state’s card services. State portals differ in the status and record searches they provide.
relationship: NFSA State Directory routes to State Card Services.

guidance: Use the official NFSA dealer directory for your state, or the nearest-shop feature in Mera Ration 2.0. Confirm shop hours or stock with the local office before travelling.
relationship: NFSA Shop Directory supports Fair Price Shop Lookup.

guidance: The official app FAQ lists nearby Fair Price Shops, entitlement information, past transactions and grievance options for beneficiaries.
relationship: Mera Ration App supports Fair Price Shop Lookup.

guidance: The Mera Ration 2.0 FAQ says the app lists previous foodgrain transactions. Use that record when checking a withdrawal before speaking to your state office.
relationship: Mera Ration App records Foodgrain Transactions.

topic: Check how much ration you can collect
guidance: Check the entitlement shown for your card in the official Mera Ration app or your state service. The card category matters when you read the monthly amount.
relationship: Mera Ration App supports Monthly Entitlement.

guidance: The NFSA specifies five kilograms per person per month for the Priority Household category. Check the registered member count and your displayed entitlement.
relationship: Priority Household Card supports Monthly Entitlement.

guidance: The NFSA specifies 35 kilograms per household per month for Antyodaya Anna Yojana. Check the card category before using this amount.
relationship: Antyodaya Card supports Monthly Entitlement.

guidance: The DFPD annual report describes free NFSA foodgrains through December 2028. If a seller asks for payment, check whether the item is your NFSA entitlement or another product and ask the official state service if needed.
relationship: Free NFSA Foodgrains supports Monthly Entitlement.

topic: Check the types of grain supplied
guidance: The ONORC FAQ says the grain mix can follow the destination state’s distribution policy. Check the entitlement display or ask the shop which grain is listed for your card.
relationship: Destination State Policy supports Grain Mix.

topic: Ask about non-supply of entitled grain
guidance: The NFSA overview describes a food security allowance provision in case entitled foodgrains or meals are not supplied. Ask the official grievance authority how it applies to your circumstances.
relationship: Food Security Allowance supports Grievance Review.

guidance: Open the NFSA state and UT directory, then choose the region responsible for your card. Use the destination state’s shop resources if the question is about where to collect grain.
relationship: NFSA State Directory supports State Food Portal.

topic: Know what a Fair Price Shop does
guidance: Fair Price Shops are distribution points in the Public Distribution System. The relevant state or UT supervises the shops and operates local distribution.
relationship: State Food Department supports Fair Price Shop Distribution.

guidance: Use the official state card service or the ration-card details feature in Mera Ration 2.0 to look up the details recorded for your card.
relationship: Mera Ration App supports State Card Services.

guidance: The NFSA PDS overview assigns supervision of Fair Price Shops and operations within a state to its authorities. Use the official state contact routes for questions about a particular shop.
relationship: State Food Department supports Local Shop Supervision.
